name: upload-dropzone
summary: A drop area for adding files: drag them in, paste them or browse, with a list of what was added and a plain reason when a file is turned away.
useWhen: People bring their own files into the product, such as reference images, source clips or a brand kit.
A form or dialog needs one or several attachments, with limits on type, size or count.

alternatives.name: add-media-panel
alternatives.when: people also pick from things already in their library, not only from their computer

alternatives.name: button
alternatives.when: one file, no preview needed: a plain Upload button that opens the file picker is enough

alternatives.name: empty-state
alternatives.when: the page is empty and uploading is only one of several ways to start

rules.do: State the accepted types and the size limit in the hint, such as "PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 20 MB each".
rules.dont: Let people find the limits out by being turned away.

rules.do: When some files in a drop are fine and some are not, add the good ones and name each one that was left out, with the reason.
rules.dont: Reject the whole drop, or show a generic "Upload failed".

rules.do: Pass `progress` while files are being sent, so each row shows how far along it is.
rules.dont: Leave a large file sitting in the list with no sign that anything is happening.

a11y: The Browse files button opens the file picker from the keyboard; the drop area is a mouse and touch shortcut, not a second tab stop.
Files turned away are announced through a live alert, each named with its reason.
Every Remove button names its file, and each progress bar is labelled with the file it belongs to.
